# Conformance fixtures — what each client actually puts on the wire

Twenty-three byte-exact messages, one per row of [`../../docs/conformance.md`](../../docs/conformance.md)
§1.1. Each is **hand-written from that client's serialisation code**, not copied from a
capture and not generated by anything in this repository — so a fixture is evidence about the
client, and a test that reads it is a claim about interoperating with that client.

⚠ **None of these came off a wire.** They are transcriptions: "Newtonsoft with
`Formatting.Indented` and `NullValueHandling.Ignore` applied to *this* DTO produces exactly
these bytes." That is enough to pin a decoder and not enough to close
[`../../docs/protocol.md`](../../docs/protocol.md) §11's unknowns. When the first real capture
exists (design §11 package 7), fixtures taken from it are promoted alongside these and marked
as captured, and any of these that turns out to be wrong is corrected with a note saying so.

## The details that are the point

Byte-for-byte is the contract. The three things a casual re-generation would get wrong:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Trailing newline** | `fb_*`, `gg_*` and `pit_*` end with `\n`; the other seventeen end with `}`. Three of sixteen clients delimit, thirteen do not, and a framer must not care either way |
| **Indentation** | `tnb_*` and `osp_*` are Newtonsoft's two spaces; `pit_*` is Boost's four; `gsp_full` and `osg_*` use tabs. A newline-splitting framer breaks on all of them |
| **Key order** | Serialiser-determined, and it differs: `osp_*` puts `APIversion` **first** because it is a public field rather than a property, and `ocr_putt` puts `ShotDataOptions` before `BallData` |

## Provenance

| File | Source | What it is here to pin |
|---|---|---|
| `gsp_full.json` | [GSP] the vendor's page, comments stripped | every field present; and its own spin numbers are internally inconsistent (CT-D15) |
| `gsp_full_commented.json` | [GSP] verbatim, **including the `//` comments** | the page's own example is not valid JSON, so somebody will paste it: it must be refused cleanly (CT-X08) |
| `tl_minimal.json` | [TL] `JSON.stringify` of an object literal | five ball keys and nothing else — ⚠ and **no `Units` key at all**, because `Units: this.unit` reads a field the constructor never set (`this.units`) and `JSON.stringify` drops `undefined`. The absent-Units case is a real client, not a hypothetical |
| `mlm_backspin.json` | [MLM] `json.dumps(device \| ball_data.to_gspro())` | `Backspin` spelled with a lower-case s; `CarryDistance` hard 0; face-to-path in `HorizontalFaceImpact` |
| `r10_apiversion.json` | [R10] `System.Text.Json`, default naming | `APIVersion` with a capital V, and **nulls written** rather than omitted |
| `r10_heartbeat.json` | [R10] `CreateHeartbeat()` | `BallData: null`, `ClubData: null`, `ShotNumber: 0` |
| `osg_float_shot_number.json` | [OSG] its own tracked sample file | `"ShotNumber": 13.0` — an integer arriving as a float — and spins with more precision than a float holds |
| `tnb_indented.json` | [TNB] Newtonsoft indented, nulls ignored | newlines and tabs **inside** one message |
| `osp_connect_heartbeat.json` | [OSP] the message it sends on connect | heartbeat and ready flag in the same message; `APIversion` first |
| `osp_shot.json` | [OSP] `SendShotData()` | nulls omitted, so `ClubData` carries `Speed` alone |
| `ocr_putt.json` | [OCR] its putting path | `SpinAxis: 0` and `VLA: 0` as deliberate placeholders on a real putt |
| `pit_shot.json` | [PIT] Boost `write_json` + its unquoting regex | ⚠ `TotalSpin: 0.0` as a placeholder beside a real `BackSpin`/`SideSpin` pair — the case that makes `gsp_ball_data_derive()` necessary |
| `pit_keepalive.json` | [PIT] `result_message_is_keepalive_` | a heartbeat that still carries full `BallData` and `ClubData` objects |
| `of_shot.json` | [OF] dataclasses → compact `json.dumps` | every member present because the dataclass defaults are `0.0` |
| `of_heartbeat.json` | [OF] `build_heartbeat()` | `LaunchMonitorBallDetected: false` carrying real state on a heartbeat |
| `ob_shot.json` | [OB] its Uneekor VIEW watcher | **`"ClubData": null`** and an extra top-level `ClubName` the protocol does not define |
| `ob_heartbeat.json` | [OB] its 3-second timer | no `BallData` or `ClubData` keys at all |
| `fb_shot_newline.json` | [FB] Go `json.Marshal` + `'\n'` | trailing newline; `omitempty` drops a zero spin pair |
| `fb_heartbeat_newline.json` | [FB] its 5-second heartbeat | `ShotNumber` **incremented per heartbeat**, not per shot |
| `gg_shot_newline.json` | [GG] serde with `skip_serializing_if` | trailing newline; a `ClubData` holding only the members that were measured |
| `gc2_shot.json` | [GC2] `serde_json::to_string` | ⚠ the unit's **serial number inside `DeviceID`**, which makes that field an identifier |
| `sb_strings.json` | [SB] a literal template with string substitution | every number and boolean as a JSON **string**, and `Apiversion` |
| `slx_zero_speed.json` | [SLX] the shape its proxy exists to filter | a "shot" with `Speed: 0` — which made GSPro reset the club selection |

Tags are [`../../docs/protocol.md`](../../docs/protocol.md) §0's.

## Adding one

1. Read the client's serialisation code, not its README, and not a capture someone posted.
2. Write the bytes it would produce, including whitespace, key order and any delimiter.
3. Add a row above naming the source and **the one thing the fixture is here to pin**. A
   fixture that duplicates another's coverage is a slower suite and no more evidence.
4. Add its `CT-` case to `docs/conformance.md` §3 and a row to §4.
5. ⚠ If it came off a real wire, redact the peer address and any serial before committing, and
   say in the row above that it is captured rather than transcribed. `.gitignore` un-excludes
   only this directory for exactly that reason.
